The document is an NDA from The Business Partnership (TBP). Let me map each hypothesis:

- nda-11: No reverse engineering — not mentioned anywhere in the document. → NotMentioned
- nda-16: Return of confidential information — Segment [26] says "shall return them to the supplying party within one week of a written request." This is about returning Confidential Information upon written request, not exactly "upon termination." But the hypothesis says "destroy or return some Confidential Information upon the termination of Agreement." The document says return upon written request. Hmm, this could be considered entailment since return is required. The phrase "upon the termination" — the document doesn't mention termination. But typically in these tasks, [26] is evidence for return of CI. I'd say Entailment with evidence [26].
- nda-15: No licensing — Agreement shall not grant Receiving Party any right to Confidential Information. Not explicitly stated. Segment [26] says materials remain property of supplying party. That suggests no rights granted. Hmm. "No licensing" typically means agreement doesn't grant rights. Not explicitly mentioned. Could be NotMentioned. But [26] "shall remain the property of the supplying party" implies no license granted. In many NDA-100 style annotations, this is often NotMentioned unless explicit. I'd lean NotMentioned.
- nda-10: Confidentiality of Agreement — not disclosing the fact that the agreement was negotiated. Not mentioned. → NotMentioned
- nda-2: None-inclusion of non-technical information — CI shall ONLY include technical information. Segment [23] defines CI broadly as "any information or data relating to any clients of The Business Partnership business or affairs." This contradicts "only technical information." → Contradiction with evidence [23].
- nda-1: Explicit identification — CI shall be expressly identified by Disclosing Party. Not mentioned; [23] defines broadly. → NotMentioned (or Contradiction?). The definition in [23] covers any information disclosed whether in writing, orally or by any other means — no marking requirement. This contradicts explicit identification requirement? The hypothesis says "All Confidential Information shall be expressly identified." The document doesn't require identification, but doesn't prohibit it either. Typically NotMentioned.
- nda-19: Survival of obligations — obligations may survive termination. Segment [29] says "this Agreement shall remain in force in perpetuity." That means obligations survive forever — entailment of survival. Evidence [29]. → Entailment.
- nda-12: Permissible development of similar information — not mentioned. → NotMentioned.
- nda-20: Permissible post-agreement possession — may retain some CI after return/destruction. Not mentioned. → NotMentioned.
- nda-3: Inclusion of verbally conveyed information — [23] "disclosed whether in writing, orally or by any other means." → Entailment, evidence [23].
- nda-18: No solicitation — Receiving Party shall not solicit Disclosing Party's representatives. Segment [27]: "I will not attempt to contact the employees, customers, creditors, suppliers or landlords of any client." That's no-contact, related to non-solicitation. Employees are representatives. → Entailment with [27]. Also [39] about staff. I'd go with [27].
- nda-7: Sharing with third-parties — may share with third parties. [25] says "not disclose it to any third party without the prior written consent." So sharing with consent is permitted. → Entailment, evidence [25]. Also [34]. I'd use [25].
- nda-17: Permissible copy — may create a copy in some circumstances. [25] says "make no copies thereof" — absolute prohibition? "Treat it as confidential and make no copies thereof not disclose it to any third party without the prior written consent" — the "without prior written consent" might apply to both copies and disclosure. Parsing: "make no copies thereof[,] not disclose it to any third party without the prior written consent of TBP and use it solely for the purpose..." Ambiguous. If consent applies to copies too, then copying with consent is permissible → Entailment. If copies are absolutely prohibited, then Contradiction. Hmm. [34] says "must not be copied or supplied to a third party without the consent of TBP" — this clearly makes copying permissible with consent. → Entailment with evidence [34] (and [25]). I'd use [25, 34] or just [34].
- nda-8: Notice on compelled disclosure — not mentioned. → NotMentioned.
- nda-13: Permissible acquirement of similar information — not mentioned. → NotMentioned.
- nda-5: Sharing with employees — may share with Receiving Party's employees. Not mentioned explicitly. [25] prohibits third-party disclosure without consent; employees of receiving party aren't addressed. → NotMentioned.
- nda-4: Limited use — shall not use CI for purposes other than stated. [25]: "use it solely for the purpose as agreed between parties." → Entailment, evidence [25].
